Because it measures flows against everything the store sells, it isolates flow performance from the store's own demand swings, so a steady share means flows are keeping pace regardless of how busy the month was.

heartbeat.title: Optimisation — the pipeline
heartbeat.body_html: No A/B tests concluded this month, so there is no single winning learning to bank this cycle. That is normal in the rhythm of testing: some months close experiments, others set them up. What carries forward is the discipline behind the numbers above, where the lift in revenue per email came from flows that earlier tests already tuned. Wins are banked permanently and losses cost nothing, so the program keeps compounding whether or not a given month posts a result.

narrative.html: Flows earned 8,398 AUD, up 35.9% on last month. More importantly, revenue per email delivered rose from 0.297 to 0.346 AUD, so the gain came from each email working harder, not just from sending more.
Flows held 15.1% of total store revenue. Against a total store take of 55,682 AUD, the automated flows we run continued to carry a steady sixth of everything the business sold this month.

Campaigns are the second lever we run, and flows remain the most efficient per-email channel. Flows earned 0.346 AUD per email versus 0.087 for campaigns, four times as much, which is exactly why flows do 84% of email revenue. Both channels are ours, and we weight effort toward what pays back hardest.
Deliverability stayed clean. Unsubscribes ran at 0.561% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.058%, well inside safe limits, which protects inbox placement for every send that follows.

heartbeat.title: Compounding without concluding a test
heartbeat.body_html: No A/B tests concluded in July, so this month's gains came from the structure already in place rather than a fresh winner. That is worth stating plainly, because it shows the flow program holds its ground and keeps growing between tests. The testing engine runs continuously in the background, banking wins permanently and costing nothing on the misses, and July's four-month climb in flow share is the payoff from that steady, low-risk optimisation.

narrative.html: Flows earned 6,763 AUD, up 64.8% on the prior month. That lifted flows to 16.5% of total store revenue, meaning roughly one dollar in six across the whole store came through the automations we manage.

The flow share of store revenue has compounded for four straight months, moving from 0.6% in April to 8.9%, then 10.7%, and now 16.5%. This is the automated channel steadily taking on more of the store's total sales rather than a one-off spike.

Flow revenue per email delivered eased to 0.325 AUD from 0.425 AUD. With total flow revenue still rising sharply, this reflects wider send volume across the audience, but we are watching per-email yield closely to keep both volume and efficiency moving in step.

Campaigns are the second lever we run, and flows remain the most efficient email we send. Flows earned 0.325 AUD per email against 0.115 AUD for campaigns, so flows return 2.8x per email, and email revenue split 73% flows to 27% campaigns across the 6 campaigns sent. Deliverability stayed clean at 0.678% unsubscribe and 0.052% spam.

heartbeat.title: No tests concluded — the program keeps compounding
heartbeat.body_html: No A/B tests reached a conclusion this month, so there are no new results to report here. The value of the testing program does not depend on any single month: every win we bank stays live permanently, while a losing variant costs nothing and is simply retired. That asymmetry means the flows compound in our favour over time at any strike rate, backed by one of the most comprehensive automated flow-testing setups in the industry. We will surface the next set of concluded tests as they land.

narrative.html: Flows grew to $4,104, up 32.3% month on month. That lifted the automated channel to 11.7% of total store revenue, meaning better than one dollar in nine across the whole store came directly from the flows we manage.

Flow revenue per email delivered eased to $0.425, down from $0.568 in May. Total flow revenue still rose, so this reflects more emails reaching more people rather than weaker performance, but it is the number we are watching to keep each send working as hard as possible.

Flows are the most efficient per-email channel we run. At $0.425 per email against $0.137 on campaigns, flows earn 3.1x more per email, and they contributed 76% of all email revenue this month. Campaigns are the second lever we run alongside them, adding reach on top of the automated base from just 3 sends.

Deliverability stayed clean. Unsubscribes ran at 0.712% of delivered and spam complaints at just 0.021%, well inside safe limits, which protects inbox placement for every flow and campaign that follows.

monthly.title_sub: Flows attributed $4,104 this month, up 32.3% on May, and held 11.7% of total store revenue.
